entries.explanation: Each key in Arguments becomes a $variable. Here Arguments is {"limit": 2}.

entries.title: Accumulate

entries.explanation: def names a filter you can reuse.

entries.explanation: Paths are lists of keys and indexes.

differences.title: Engine
differences.detail: Filters run on a Swift engine built for this app, which follows jq 1.7.1. Each build is checked against jq 1.7.1's own test suite and more than 1,300 filters whose output was recorded from real jq 1.7.1. Filters written for jq 1.7 behave the same way.

differences.title: Files and the environment are off
differences.detail: input, inputs, input_filename, env, $ENV, include, import, modulemeta, get_search_list, get_prog_origin and get_jq_origin are removed, so a filter cannot read files or environment variables. A filter that uses one stops with an error that names it. Turn on Slurp to see every input value at once, and use Arguments to pass values in. builtins does not list the removed functions, and input_line_number always returns 0.

differences.title: Limits
differences.detail: Every run stops at its timeout and at a memory limit, and very deep recursion stops with an error instead of crashing. A regular expression that backtracks on long text stops at the timeout.

differences.title: Regular expressions
differences.detail: jq uses the Oniguruma library; this app uses ICU, the library behind Apple's regular expressions. The patterns on this cheat sheet and jq's own regex tests work the same in both. Rarely used syntax can differ, so try a complex pattern in the Playground before you rely on it.

differences.title: halt_error, debug and stderr
differences.detail: halt ends the run and keeps the results so far. halt_error stops the action with its message as the error text. debug and stderr appear in the Playground's Debug area, and Shortcuts ignores them.

differences.title: Results in Shortcuts
differences.detail: Shortcuts receives every result as Text. Objects and lists arrive as JSON text, which Get Dictionary Value and the other dictionary actions read directly. Numbers, true, false and null arrive as their JSON text. With One item per result, a single list result is split into its items.

differences.title: Dates
differences.detail: strftime, strptime, mktime, gmtime, todate and fromdate work in UTC, as in jq. localtime and strflocaltime use the time zone of your device.

differences.title: Error messages
differences.detail: Errors are reworded to name the position or value involved and a next step. The text jq prints, such as Cannot iterate over null, is still part of each message.
